rename.from: Overriding signs in the new diagnostic
rename.to: Overriding signs in the new diagnostic namespace?

body: I faced the same issue here today after rebuild to the latest master. I have migrated most of my setup to a new API, but sign definitions are getting overridden as state in the original issue above.

> The signs are defined whenever the diagnostics are displayed for the first time, so overriding it is very tricky.
> 
> I'm using a weird workaround for now:

what is non-workaround sample code that you expect to work?

Related, docs conflict on how to define the respective signs:

`:h diagnostic-signs`

```viml
	sign define DiagnosticSignError text=E texthl=DiagnosticSignError linehl= numhl=
	sign define DiagnosticSignWarning text=W texthl=DiagnosticSignWarning linehl= numhl=
	sign define DiagnosticSignInformation text=I texthl=DiagnosticSignInformation linehl= numhl=
	sign define DiagnosticSignHint text=H texthl=DiagnosticSignHint linehl= numhl=
```

whereas `:h diagnostic-highlight`

```viml
						*hl-DiagnosticSignError*
DiagnosticSignError
  Used for "Error" signs in sign column.

						*hl-DiagnosticSignWarn*
DiagnosticSignWarn
  Used for "Warn" signs in sign column.

						*hl-DiagnosticSignInfo*
DiagnosticSignInfo
  Used for "Info" signs in sign column.

						*hl-DiagnosticSignHint*
DiagnosticSignHint
  Used for "Hint" signs in sign column.
```

A non-workaround sample code on my end would be for something like the below to work wherever I define highlights and signs at neovim startup (signs might be incorrectly shown as my brower fonts are a bit borked). Apologies if I missed something here in the docs. 

```lua
local signs = { "", "", "", "" }
local diagnostic_types = { "Error", "Warn", "Info", "Hint" } -- or Warning, Information (which also don't seem to work) ... 
for i = 1, #diagnostic_types do
  local diagnostic_type = string.format("DiagnosticSign%s", diagnostic_types[i])
  local opts = {
    text = signs[i],
    texthl = string.format("Diagnostic%s", diagnostic_types[i]),
    linehl = "",
    numhl = "",
  }
  vim.fn.sign_define(diagnostic_type, opts)
end
```

Another related change:  `vim.diagnostic.severity` now defines severity groups in capital letters (`ERROR`) whereas `vim.lsp.protocol.DiagnosticSeverity` only capitalizes the first letter (`Error`) as per [spec](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/specification-3-17/#diagnosticSeverity). Ignore if this is an intentional change.

> > The signs are defined whenever the diagnostics are displayed for the first time, so overriding it is very tricky.
> > 
> > I'm using a weird workaround for now:
> 
> what is non-workaround sample code that you expect to work?

Previously, I was able to simply define them, like in init.lua.

I think it makes sense that neovim defines the default ones: it's a resource owned by core. Perhaps the user could customize the sign names, maybe passing as a config to the on_publish_diagnostics handler?

Then _set_signs would take that as a parameter and create and use the default ones whenever the parameter is omitted.

Alternatively, we could introduce a boolean flag telling _set_signs to not define the default signs (and pass that via on_publish_diagnostics), but idk boolean flags are pretty much always a smell.

issue.title: `DiagnosticSign*` signs are reverted to default values when first lsp diagnostic is displayed.

repository.name: neovim
repository.description: Vim-fork focused on extensibility and usability

issue.body:
### Neovim version (nvim -v)

v0.6.0-dev+286-g4881456e8

### Vim (not Nvim) behaves the same?

no

### Operating system/version

ArchLinux

### Terminal name/version

urxvt v9.26

### $TERM environment variable

xterm-256color

### Installation

AUR repository (neovim-git)

### How to reproduce the issue

Open Nvim with configured lsp.

`:sign define DiagnosticSignError text=X texthl=DiagnosticSignError linehl= numhl=`

`sign list DiagnosticSignError` will produce:
`sign DiagnosticSignError text=X  linehl= texthl=DiagnosticSignError numhl=`

Without closing neovim open file with lsp error.
`sign list DiagnosticSignError` will produce:
`sign DiagnosticSignError text=E  linehl= texthl=DiagnosticSignError numhl=`

### Expected behavior

Keep X as text sign for lsp errors.

### Actual behavior

X is overriden by default E sign for lsp errors.

Only happens when first error is displayed, if I change sign after that everything works as expected.
